chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ubayda al-Wasiti, from Ajlan, who said:

I had dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) after darkness, and he used to have dinner after darkness. So vinegar, oil, and cold meat were brought to him. He began to pick at the meat and feed it to me, while he himself ate the vinegar and the oil and left the meat. He said: 'This is our food, and the food of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of vinegar and oil in Shia tradition according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) exemplifies the Prophetic tradition of simplicity by consuming vinegar and oil while offering richer food to his companion, thereby establishing these humble items as the sustenance of the Ahl al-Bayt. This act underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) and the spiritual purity derived from modest dietary habits, linking the Imams directly to the lineage of the Prophets through their daily practices.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ubeyda Al Wasity, from Ajlan who said,

‘I had dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> after darkness, and he<sup>asws</sup> tended to have dinner after darkness. So they came with vinegar, and oil, and cold meat, so he<sup>asws</sup> went on to pluck the meat and feed it, and he<sup>asws</sup> (himself) would eat the vinegar, and the oil, and leave the meat. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is our<sup>asws</sup> meal, and a meal of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Ubaydah al-Wasitiy from ‘Ajlan who has said the following:

“I once had dinner with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, after Salat (prayer) of al-‘Isha’. He (the Imam) would take dinner after Salat (prayer) of al-‘Isha’. Vinegar, oil and cold meat were brought. He began to pull pieces of meat and give them to me but himself eat vinegar and oil and left the meat. He (the Imam) said, ‘This is our food and the food of the prophets ‘Alayhim al-Salam.’”
